title: Hidden content-provider package names stale: MediaProvider is a Mainline module since Android 11
description: HidingUtil.lockdownNow()/endLockdown() hide/show hardcoded com.android.providers.media, com.android.externalstorage, com.android.providers.downloads, com.android.traceur. Since Android 11, MediaProvider ships as Mainline module (com.google.android.providers.media.module on Google builds; OEM/GrapheneOS names differ). Hiding the legacy name likely fails silently -> sensitive work-profile media remains browsable in lockdown (thesis fig. 3.3 behavior broken). Fix: resolve provider packages dynamically (PackageManager.resolveContentProvider for MediaStore.AUTHORITY etc.) instead of hardcoding; add test.

title: Lockdown storage-permission revocation is obsolete under scoped storage (SDK 36)
description: HidingUtil.disableStoragePermissions() denies only READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE. On API 33+ media access uses READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/VIDEO/AUDIO (+ READ_MEDIA_VISUAL_USER_SELECTED on 34+); WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is a no-op for targetSdk>=30; MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE apps are untouched. Result: lockdown no longer blocks media/file access as thesis sec. 3.5.2 intends — security regression. Fix: extend deny list to modern media permissions, handle All-Files-Access, and confirm PERMISSION_POLICY_AUTO_DENY covers them; restore symmetrically in endLockdown().

title: Unset wipe/lockdown thresholds default to -1: single failed PIN can trigger wipe
description: AppSettings.getPreferenceInt() defaults to -1. In DueProcessDeviceAdminReceiver.onPasswordFailed(), 'attempts >= threshold' with threshold -1 is always true, so enabling WIPE_TRIGGER/LOCKDOWN_TRIGGER before the seekbar pref is ever written makes ONE mistyped device PIN wipe the work profile. Also: code TODO notes lockdown trigger fires repeatedly when already in lockdown. Fix: validated defaults (and refuse to arm trigger without explicit threshold), guard against re-triggering, unit tests for the threshold matrix.

title: Unlock pattern stored in plaintext SharedPreferences (thesis 7.1.1 known gap)
description: AppSettings stores the pattern (UNLOCK_CODE, auth_prefs) and sensitive-app list in cleartext; code carries TODO 'Make secure prefs'. Thesis 7.1.1 explicitly flags this: [T4] access exposes both the unlock secret and the list of apps marked sensitive. Pattern space is tiny (>=108 combos, 4*3^(n-1)) so the stored value must never be recoverable: store a salted, stretched hash (PBKDF2/Argon2) verified on input, bind salt/key to Android Keystore, and consider EncryptedSharedPreferences for SENSITIVE_APPS/STORAGE_GRANTED_APPS sets.

title: Provisioning uses deprecated ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE + startActivityForResult
description: SetupFragment launches DevicePolicyManager.ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE via startActivityForResult. The action is deprecated (Android 12+ guidance: provisioning via platform-managed flows) and startActivityForResult is deprecated in favor of Activity Result API. Verify work-profile provisioning end-to-end on SDK 36 device/emulator; migrate to current DPC provisioning path. Also evaluate thesis 7.1.1 suggestion EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SKIP_EDUCATION_SCREENS while touching this code.

title: Verify invisible pattern-unlock overlay still works on Android 12-16 (window context + untrusted-touch blocking)
description: PatternUnlock adds a TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY view via WindowManager obtained from a BroadcastReceiver context (DueProcessDeviceAdminReceiver BOOT_COMPLETED). Android 11+ expects Context.createWindowContext for non-activity windows (getDefaultDisplay() also deprecated); Android 12 blocks untrusted touch events passing through overlays, which the pass-through pattern input depends on (FLAG_NOT_TOUCH_MODAL/FLAG_SPLIT_TOUCH). The entire lockdown-recovery mechanism (thesis 3.6.2) is at risk on SDK 36. Action: instrumented test on Android 14-16 emulator; migrate to window context; if pass-through is blocked, redesign recovery (see Private Space / quiet-mode beads).

title: Update README with isolated Android build setup instructions for Debian Trixie
description:
Provide concrete steps in README.md for setting up a developer build environment on Debian Trixie (testing):
1. Install OpenJDK 21 via apt: sudo apt install openjdk-21-jdk
2. Download and extract Android Command Line Tools into an isolated directory (e.g., ~/.local/share/android-sdk).
3. Use sdkmanager to install platform SDK 36 and build-tools 36.
4. Set environment variables (ANDROID_HOME, JAVA_HOME) to point to the isolated paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] README.md contains a section detailing installation steps on Debian Trixie.
- [ ] The instructions outline installing openjdk-21-jdk.
- [ ] The instructions describe downloading the command-line tools and installing platforms/build-tools under a user-local isolated directory.

title: Lockdown recovery UX: 5/6 usability-study participants failed recovery (thesis task 7)
description: Thesis 5.2.3: recovery after lockdown (toggle work profile, wait for boot broadcast, draw invisible pattern) was failed by all but one participant, mostly due to timing of the pattern start. Mitigations from thesis 7.1.1: first-time guided pop-up walkthrough, intro video, and (platform-level) quiet-mode request to skip the off/on toggle. Implement first-run guided recovery rehearsal + some perceivable readiness cue that does not hurt plausibility (e.g. require pattern start only after overlay actually attached; optional haptic tick).

title: Evaluate Android 15+ Private Space vs/with Due Process work-profile approach
description: Android 15 introduced Private Space: a native hidden profile with separate lock, hidden-from-launcher state and its own keys — overlapping much of thesis ch. 2.5/3 (work-profile hiding). Assess: (1) can Due Process target or manage a Private Space profile; (2) does Private Space's existence change the plausibility story (everyone has the feature => deniability improves, per thesis 'blend in' argument); (3) which Due Process features remain unique (inconspicuous lockscreen-fail trigger, silent wipe, policy hardening, decoy lockscreen). Output: positioning/architecture decision doc + follow-up beads.

title: Re-audit plausibility surfaces on Android 14-16
description: Thesis 5.1.2 catalogued giveaways on Android 10: 'not installed for this user' in Settings app list, work-profile storage usage, overlay ('displaying over other apps') notification, dumpsys user/package output, unique restriction set fingerprint. Android 12-16 changed work-profile UI substantially (pause UX, Settings redesign, Private Space coexistence). Re-run the [T1]-[T3] forensic walkthrough from the thesis on SDK 36 hardware, document which leaks remain/appeared, and feed results into lockdown action list.

title: PostProvisioningTask hardcodes Google packages; crashes/no-ops on AOSP-like builds (e.g. GrapheneOS)
description: installDefaultApps() calls enableSystemApp for com.android.vending, com.android.chrome, com.google.android.gm. enableSystemApp throws IllegalArgumentException when the package is absent (GrapheneOS, AOSP, many OEMs) — post-provisioning then aborts before HidingUtil icon swap and setPostProvisioningDone(), leaving setup broken. Also REMOVE_GOOGLE_ACCOUNT path hides com.google.android.gms which does not exist there. Wrap per-package in try/catch, detect available packages, make default-app set configurable.

title: Enable R8 minify/obfuscation and strip logging in release builds
description: Thesis 5.1.2: resource-ids leak via UI dump (fig. 5.2) and logcat output lets [T3] fingerprint the app even with renamed packages; thesis says 'thorough obfuscation is definitely necessary'. app/build.gradle has minifyEnabled false and code contains Log.d calls (AppSettings, PostProvisioningTask, etc.). Enable R8 with obfuscation + resource shrinking for release, strip Log.* via proguard -assumenosideeffects, audit remaining string constants (e.g. 'DueProcessDeviceAdminReceiver' TAG) for fingerprintability.

title: Harden pattern-unlock tarpit: wall-clock based, logic duplicated
description: Tarpit (thesis 3.6.2) uses System.currentTimeMillis() with an ACTION_TIME_CHANGED compensation hack; wall clock is adversary-influenced (network time, timezone). Use SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() plus persisted boot marker for monotonic lockout. Tarpit/attempt logic is also duplicated between DueProcessDeviceAdminReceiver and the MainActivity lockscreen path — extract one shared, unit-tested implementation. Consider exponential backoff and cap.

title: Verify parent-profile DPM calls under modern restrictions (biometrics keyguard, failed-attempt count)
description: lockdownNow() calls getParentProfileInstance().setKeyguardDisabledFeatures(KEYGUARD_DISABLE_BIOMETRICS) to kill personal-profile biometrics, and onPasswordFailed() reads getParentProfileInstance().getCurrentFailedPasswordAttempts(). Since Android 11/12, several parent-instance APIs are limited to organization-owned managed profiles; a plain PO may get SecurityException or silent no-op. Lockscreen-fail triggering (thesis 3.5.1) and biometric hardening depend on these. Verify on SDK 36; add graceful degradation + user-visible capability report.

title: Thesis conformance review: implementation vs MScThesis (Gründling 2020)
description: Review of docs/MScThesis_BernhardGründling.pdf against the modernize branch (SDK 36). VERDICT: implementation faithfully matches thesis ch.3 design — PO-mode DPC, work profile, lockdown/wipe with lockscreen-fail + in-app triggers, invisible 4-corner pattern unlock with tarpit, content-provider hiding, storage-permission revocation, FLAG_SECURE, allowBackup=false, activity-alias relabel, key-eviction option. BUT thesis assumes Android 10 (API 29); the branch now targets SDK 36 and several thesis-era mechanisms have decayed or are unverified on modern Android. Child beads (discovered-from this one) hold individual findings: security regressions, deprecated APIs, plausibility surfaces, and thesis ch.7 future-work items.

title: Thesis ch.7 future-work backlog: APK generator, quiet-mode recovery, secondary lockscreen, profile rename
description: Tracking bead for remaining thesis 7.1 items not covered elsewhere: (1) web service generating per-user APKs (package name, labels, icon randomized) to defeat fingerprinting — thesis 4.1; (2) UserManager.requestQuietModeEnabled-based recovery if permission landscape changed (MODIFY_QUIET_MODE was signature-only on A10 — recheck on 14-16); (3) DPM secondary-lockscreen API (appeared in R DP3, later removed — check if a stable equivalent exists now); (4) renameable profile label via setProfileName already used — review wording ('work profile' vs neutral). Split into child beads when picked up.
